# Draft Outlook replies faster with Meta AI

If your inbox fills up every morning and you spend more time typing “Thanks for your email” than you do on real work, this guide is for you. You’ll learn how to use Meta AI inside Outlook to draft quick, polite replies in seconds, so you can hit send without rewriting every message.

## Before you start
- A **free Microsoft Outlook account** (web, desktop or mobile)
- A **Meta AI account** (free at [meta.ai](https://meta.ai))
- Roughly **10 minutes** of your time
- A device with a web browser or the Outlook app installed

---

## Step 1 — Open Outlook and start a new reply
Open Outlook on your computer or phone and open any email you want to reply to. Look for a button like **Reply**, **Reply all** or **Forward** at the top of the message. Tap or click it to start a new reply window.
A blank reply box appears with the cursor ready to type.
If you don’t see a reply button, look for a curved arrow icon or a menu with three dots labeled **More actions**.
You'll know it worked when you see a new reply box ready for typing.

💬 Example:
Open Outlook → open an email → click **Reply**.

---

## Step 2 — Ask Meta AI to draft your reply
Inside the reply box, type a short instruction for Meta AI. Keep it simple: “Meta AI, draft a polite reply saying I’ll get back to them tomorrow.” Press **Enter** or the send icon.
Meta AI shows a draft reply below your message in a light grey box.
If the draft doesn’t appear, check that you’re signed in to Meta AI in the same browser tab.
You'll know it worked when you see a grey box with a ready-to-use reply.

💬 Example:
Meta AI, draft a polite reply saying I’ll get back to them tomorrow.

---

## Step 3 — Review the draft and tweak if needed
Read the Meta AI draft in the grey box. If it’s too formal, too short or misses a key detail, add a sentence like “keep it friendly and mention the document I’ll send.” Press **Enter** again to refresh the draft.
Meta AI updates the reply in the same grey box with your new instructions.
If nothing changes, try rephrasing your request with more detail.
You'll know it worked when the reply box shows a new, updated draft that matches your tone.

💬 Example:
keep it friendly and mention the document I’ll send

---

## Step 4 — Copy the draft into your reply
Click inside the grey draft box, then press **Ctrl+C** (Windows) or **Cmd+C** (Mac) to copy the text. Click back into the main reply box and press **Ctrl+V** or **Cmd+V** to paste it.
The draft text appears in the reply box, ready for you to send.
If the paste doesn’t work, right-click in the reply box and choose **Paste**.
You'll know it worked when the reply box contains the full draft text you just copied.

💬 Example:
[Paste the text here]

---

## Step 5 — Add your signature and send
Scroll to the bottom of the reply box and check that your name and signature appear. If they’re missing, look for a link like **Insert signature** or **Signature** in the toolbar. Click it to add yours.
The email now has your signature and the Meta AI draft text.
If the signature doesn’t appear, your Outlook settings may need updating.
You'll know it worked when the email looks complete with your signature and the draft text.

💬 Example:
Click **Insert signature** if needed.

---

## Common mistakes
- **Meta AI doesn’t show a draft** → Make sure you’re signed in to Meta AI in the same browser tab and you pressed Enter after typing your request.
- **Draft is too formal or too casual** → Add a sentence like “keep it friendly and mention the document I’ll send” and press Enter again to refresh.
- **Signature is missing** → Look for **Insert signature** in the toolbar and click it before sending.

---

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Spend less time typing the same polite phrases and more time on the work that matters.
- **For your business or work:** Keep your replies consistent and professional without slowing down your day.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with one email today — open Outlook, reply to any message, and ask Meta AI for a draft.

---

## Try it now
Open Outlook, reply to any email, type “Meta AI, draft a polite reply saying I’ll get back to them tomorrow,” press Enter, copy the draft, and send it. That’s it—you’ve just saved two minutes.
